subject: Some questions about the Generalized Graded Unfolding Model

messages.author: 9403604069d4685f
messages.subject: Some questions about the Generalized Graded Unfolding Model
parts:
Dear Phil,

I am using the mirt package to analyze some questionnaire response data under the GGUM. I have several questions that I was hoping you could help me with:

1.) In the original paper where the model is described (http://www.ets.org/Media/Research/pdf/RR-98-32.pdf), in Figure 2 which shows the item tracelines, the x-axis is labelled as θ - δ. However, when using mirt to apply GGUM to scales from several questionnaires, the x-axis is labelled θ, although the curves generally follow the same shape as the curves in the original paper and it appears that they are using the same scale. I was wondering who is wrong here - for now I think that the original authors are wrong, since I think they incorrectly labelled the x-axis on the Figure 3. That figure shows the item characteristic curve and the x-axis is also labelled as θ - δ, although from what I understand the approximate quadratic shape of the item characteristic curve in GGUM should be a function of θ, not θ - δ. Can you clarify that it is the original authors who are wrong here (i.e., that they incorrectly labelled Figures 2 and 3, and not just the Figure 3)?

2.) I am dealing with the case where I'm unsure if the data conforms to the unidimensional unfolding model, or the two-dimensional linear (or at least, monotonic) model. In literature this is known as the "extra-factor phenomenon". I found a paper which explains that it is not possible to discern between the two models at the covariance-structure level (http://journals.sagepub.com/doi/pdf/10.1177/01466216010251006). However, the paper goes on, if the data conforms to the unidimensional unfolding model, and not to the linear/monotonic model, and if it is analyzed through linear exploratory factor analysis with 2 factors, the scatterplot of the Bartlett factor scores of the two factors should be a (possibly rotated) parabola. 

I simulated some data with mirt under the GGUM model using the simdata function and followed the procedure described above. However, the scatterplot of the Bartlett factor scores of the two factors doesn't quite resemble a parabola, although it does look like some sort of a concave curve. Do you have any thoughts on what could be going on here? Please see the image attached.

On Thu, Jul 26, 2018 at 11:46 AM AM <mut...@gmail.com> wrote:
Dear Phil,

I am using the mirt package to analyze some questionnaire response data under the GGUM. I have several questions that I was hoping you could help me with:

1.) In the original paper where the model is described (http://www.ets.org/Media/Research/pdf/RR-98-32.pdf), in Figure 2 which shows the item tracelines, the x-axis is labelled as θ - δ. However, when using mirt to apply GGUM to scales from several questionnaires, the x-axis is labelled θ, although the curves generally follow the same shape as the curves in the original paper and it appears that they are using the same scale. I was wondering who is wrong here - for now I think that the original authors are wrong, since I think they incorrectly labelled the x-axis on the Figure 3. That figure shows the item characteristic curve and the x-axis is also labelled as θ - δ, although from what I understand the approximate quadratic shape of the item characteristic curve in GGUM should be a function of θ, not θ - δ. Can you clarify that it is the original authors who are wrong here (i.e., that they incorrectly labelled Figures 2 and 3, and not just the Figure 3)?

I think they are both right. mirt's label indicates that the point of 0 probability occurs somewhere along theta, not necessarily where theta = 0, while Roberts just translates the x-axis to be centered right at the value of 0 by subtracting out the respective intercept terms. Hence, their graphic is just a shift in the x-axis.

2.) I am dealing with the case where I'm unsure if the data conforms to the unidimensional unfolding model, or the two-dimensional linear (or at least, monotonic) model. In literature this is known as the "extra-factor phenomenon". I found a paper which explains that it is not possible to discern between the two models at the covariance-structure level (http://journals.sagepub.com/doi/pdf/10.1177/01466216010251006). However, the paper goes on, if the data conforms to the unidimensional unfolding model, and not to the linear/monotonic model, and if it is analyzed through linear exploratory factor analysis with 2 factors, the scatterplot of the Bartlett factor scores of the two factors should be a (possibly rotated) parabola. 

I simulated some data with mirt under the GGUM model using the simdata function and followed the procedure described above. However, the scatterplot of the Bartlett factor scores of the two factors doesn't quite resemble a parabola, although it does look like some sort of a concave curve. Do you have any thoughts on what could be going on here? Please see the image attached.

I don't think I'm familiar enough with the theory/reasoning of this method to offer anything meaningful. Perhaps others on this forum who are more familiar with the GGUM can offer some interpretation of this phenomenon?

Phil
